questions.question: I helped her solve the problem.(Passive)[]
options: She was helped to solve the problem.
The problem was solved by me.
Her problem was solved by me.
She was helped to solve the problem by me.
questions.explanation:
The sentence is in the Simple Past tense (helped). When converting to passive, the object (her) becomes the subject (She).The bare infinitive (solve) in the active voice must change to a full infinitive (to solve) in the passive voice.
âStructure: Subject + was/were + helped + to + Verb + by + Agent.

questions.question: He saw me do it.[]
options: I was seen do it by him.
I was seen to do it by him.
I was seen doing it by him.
I was seen to doing it by him.
questions.explanation:
This sentence uses a verb of perception (saw).In the active voice,these are followed by a bare infinitive(do).However,in the passive voice, they require a "to" infinitive (to do).The object (me) becomes the subject (I),and the past tense verb (saw) becomes was seen.
âStructure: Subject + was/were + seen + to + Verb + by + Agent.

questions.question: Never tell a lie.[]
options: Let never a lie be told.
Let not a lie never be told.
Let a lie never be told.
Let lie never be told.
questions.explanation: This is a negative imperative sentence. When using "Never", the passive structure follows the pattern: Let + never + object + be + V3

questions.question: Never a tell a lie.[]
options: Let not a lie ever be told.
Let a lie never be told.
Let a lie not ever be told.
Let never be told a lie.
questions.explanation: This is a negative imperative sentence. When using "Never", the passive structure follows the pattern: Let + never + object + be + V3

questions.question: Do you know him ? (Passive)[]
options: Is he known by you ?
Is he known to you ?
Does he known by you ?
Is he known with you ?
questions.explanation:
The "Know" Rule: Unlike most verbs that use "by" (e.g., done by, seen by), the verb know must be followed by "to".
âStructure: Is/Am/Are + Subject + known + to + Agent?

questions.question: Do you find your payment too little ? (Passive)[]
options: Is your payment found too little to you ?
Are your payment found too little to you ?
Are your payment found too little by you ?
Is your payment found too little by you ?
questions.explanation:
This is an Interrogative sentence in the Simple Present tense.Unlike the verb "know" (which uses to),the verb "find" follows the standard rule of using "by" for the agent.
âStructure: Is/Am/Are + Object + Past Participle (V3) + Adjective + by + Subject

questions.question: Some Children are helping the wounded man.[]
options: The wounded man was helped by some Children.
The wounded man was helping by some Children.
The wounded man was to be helped by some Children.
The wounded man is being helped by some Children.
questions.explanation:
âThis sentence is in the Present Continuous tense (are helping). To keep the "continuous" meaning in the passive voice, we must use the word "being".
âStructure: Object + is/am/are + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject

questions.question: He is going to give me a prize.[]
options: I am going to give a prize by him.
I am gone to give a prize by him.
I was going to be given a prize by him.
I am going to be given a prize by him.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses the "going to" future construction followed by an infinitive (give). In passive voice, the "going to" part remains the same, but the infinitive changes to be + V3.

questions.question: The gate was opened by the poem.[]
options: The poem opened the gate.
The poem had opened the gate.
The poem has opened the gate.
The poem opens the gate.
questions.explanation:
This is a Passive to Active conversion.The sentence is in the Simple Past passive form (was opened).
âStructure (Passive): Object + was/were + V3 + by + Agent
âStructure (Active): Agent + Past Tense Verb (V2) + Object

questions.question: They laugh at us.[]
options: We are laugh at them.
We are laughed at with them.
We are laughed by them.
We are laughed at by them.
questions.explanation:
This involves a Phrasal Verb (laugh at). In the passive voice, the preposition (at) must remain attached to the verb.
âStructure: Object + am/is/are + Past Participle (V3) + Preposition + by + Subject

questions.question: Shelia was writing a letter.[]
options: A letter was writing by Shelia.
A letter was being written by Shelia.
A letter was being writing by Shelia.
A letter was been written by Shelia.
questions.explanation:
To keep the "continuous" aspect in passive voice, you must use the word "being".
âStructure: Object + was/were + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject

questions.question: He taught me to read Arabic.[]
options: I was taught by him to read Arabic.
I have been taught by him to read Arabic.
I had been taught by him to read Arabic.
I was being taught to read Arabic.
questions.explanation:
This sentence is in the Simple Past tense (taught). It contains a direct object (Arabic) and an indirect object (me).
âStructure: Subject (Person) + was/were + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent + Infinitive phrase

questions.question: He made me drive the car.[]
options: I was made drive his car by him.
I was made to drive his car by him.
I was made driven his car by him.
I am made to drive his car by him.
questions.explanation:
This involves the Causative Verb "make." In the active voice, "make" is followed by a bare infinitive (verb without "to").In the passive voice, it must change to a full infinitive (verb with "to").
âStructure: Subject + was/were + made + to + Verb + Object + by + Agent

questions.question: Who has broken the glass ? (Passive)[]
options: Who was broken the glass ?
By whom was the glass broken ?
By whom has the glass broken ?
By whom has the glass been broken ?
questions.explanation:
Questions starting with "Who" change to "By whom" in the passive voice.
âStructure: By whom + has/have + object + been + Past Participle (V3)?

questions.question: Do not laugh at the poor (passive)[]
options: Let the poor be not laughed at.
Let the poor be laughed at.
Let the poor be not laugh at.
Let the poor be laugh at.
questions.explanation:
For negative commands (Do not), we use the Let structure.
The preposition "at" is part of the verb phrase (laugh at) and must stay attached to the verb in the passive voice.
âStructure: Let + Object + be + not + V3 + Preposition

questions.question: We made her recite a poem.[]
options: A poem was made recite by her.
She was made to recite a poem.
She was made recited a poem.
A poem was made to be recited.
questions.explanation:
In active voice, the verb "make" is followed by a bare infinitive (recite). In passive voice, it must change to a full infinitive (to recite).
âStructure: Subject + was/were + made + to + Verb + Object + by + Agent

questions.question: Did the boy catch the bird ?[]
options: Was the bird caught by the boy ?
Was the bird being caught by the boy ?
Is the bird caught by the boy ?
Has the bird been caught by the boy ?
questions.explanation: This is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Past tense. To convert it to passive voice, we use the structure: Was/Were + subject (the bird) + past participle (caught) + by + agent (the boy)?

questions.question: BBC broadcast the news.[]
options: The news are broadcasted by BBC.
The news are broadcast by BBC.
The news is broadcast by BBC.
The news was broadcast by BBC.
questions.explanation: In this context,"broadcast" is used as a Simple Past verb. Even though the word "news" looks plural,it is grammatically uncountable and singular.Therefore,we use the auxiliary "was" + the past participle "broadcast" (which remains the same in all three forms).

questions.question: Who broke the pencil ?[]
options: By whom the pencil was broken ?
By whom was the pencil broken ?
The pencil was broken by whom ?
Who was broken the pencil ?
questions.explanation: When an active sentence starts with "Who", it usually changes to "By whom" in the passive voice. Since the sentence is in the Simple Past, we use the structure: By whom + was/were + object (the pencil) + past participle (broken)?

questions.question: Let the book be read by you.[]
options: Read the book.
You are to read the book.
Let the book read by you.
Let the book be reading by you.
questions.explanation: This is a conversion from passive to active voice for an imperative sentence (a command). The passive structure "Let + object + be + V3" is the standard way to represent a direct command like "Read the book" in passive form.

questions.question: Who will help you ?[]
options: By whom will you be helped ?
By whom you will be helped ?
By whom would you be helped ?
By whom will be you helped ?
questions.explanation:
For interrogative sentences starting with "Who" in the Simple Future tense, the passive structure is: By whom + will + object (you) + be + V3 (helped)? 
Note that the auxiliary "will" must come before the subject "you" to maintain the question format.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: The matter was informed in the police.
The matter had been informed of the police.
The police were informed of the matter.
The police was informed of the matter.
questions.explanation: In English grammar, the word "police" is a collective noun that is always treated as plural. Therefore, it requires the plural auxiliary verb "were" rather than the singular "was." Additionally, the correct preposition to use with "informed" in this context is "of."

questions.question: He did not tell the dangerous secret to anybody.[]
options: The dangerous secret was not told to anybody by him.
The dangerous secret was not told to him by anybody.
The dangerous secret was told not him to anybody.
Anybody was not told about the dangerous secret by him.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Simple Past (Negative). The passive structure is: Object (The dangerous secret) + was not + V3 (told) + to anybody + by + agent (him).

questions.question: We insist on punctuality in this office.[]
options: Punctuality is insisted on in this office.
Punctuality be insisted in this office.
Punctuality should be insisted in this office.
Punctuality is to be insisted on in this office.
questions.explanation: This is in the Simple Present tense. When a verb is followed by a fixed preposition (like insist on), that preposition must stay with the verb in the passive voice. The structure is: Subject (Punctuality) + is + V3 (insisted) + on + remaining part of the sentence.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: By whom it is painted ?
By whom it is painted with ?
Who was it painted by ?
With whom it is painted by ?
questions.explanation: This is a passive question. While "By whom" is formally correct, the structure in option A is missing the question word order (it should be "By whom is it painted?"). Option C uses the common modern structure: Who + auxiliary verb + subject + V3 + preposition (by)?

questions.question: Don't take the forget me not.[]
options: Forget me not be taken by you.
Let not the forget me not be taken by you.
Let never taken the forget me not.
Let not taken by you the forget me not.
questions.explanation: This is a negative imperative sentence. The standard passive formula for a "Don't..." command is: Let + not + object (the forget me not) + be + V3 (taken).

questions.question: Who is calling me ?[]
options: By whom I am called ?
By whom I am being called ?
By whom am I being called ?
By whom have I being called ?
questions.explanation: This is in the Present Continuous tense. The passive structure for "Who" is: By whom + am/is/are + object (I) + being + V3 (called)?

questions.question: Buy me a shirt.[]
options: Let a shirt be bought.
Let a shirt be bought for me.
Let bought a shirt for me.
Let buy a shirt for me.
questions.explanation: This is an imperative sentence with a direct object (a shirt) and an indirect object (me). The standard passive form is: Let + direct object (a shirt) + be + V3 (bought) + for + indirect object (me).

questions.question: I know him.[]
options: He was known to me.
He is known to me.
I was known to him.
He known to me.
questions.explanation: In the Simple Present, "know" changes to "is known." Crucially, the verb "know" takes the preposition "to" in the passive voice instead of the usual "by.

questions.question: Who did it ?[]
options: By whom had it been done ?
By whom was it done ?
Who is it done by ?
By whom has it been done ?
questions.explanation: This is in the Simple Past. The structure is: By whom + was/were + object (it) + V3 (done)?

questions.question: He has a cow.[]
options: A cow is had by him.
A cow is have by him.
A cow have been by him.
A cow has been by him.
questions.explanation: In the Simple Present, the verb "has" (possession) is converted to the passive form "is had." The object "a cow" becomes the subject, followed by the auxiliary verb "is" and the past participle "had."

questions.question: What is wanted by him ?[]
options: What do he want ?
What did he want ?
What does he want ?
What is he wants ?
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Present passive question. To convert it to active, use the interrogative structure: What + do/does + subject (he) + base verb (want)?

questions.question: I was brightly addressed by her.[]
options: She addressed me brightly.
She has addressed me brightly.
She addresses me brightly.
I was addressed by her brightly.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the Simple Past passive ("was addressed"). To change it to active, the agent "her" becomes the subject "She," followed by the past tense verb "addressed" and the object "me."

questions.question: Let us write a letter.[]
options: Let a letter to write by us.
Let a letter be wrote by us.
Let a letter be written by us.
Let a letter written by us.
questions.explanation: For "Let us..." imperative sentences, the passive structure is: Let + object (a letter) + be + V3 (written) + by + us.

questions.question: You will be helped by me ?[]
options: I shall help you.
I must help you.
I shall have helped you.
I should help you.
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Future passive sentence. In the active voice, the subject "I" typically pairs with the auxiliary "shall" (or "will"), followed by the base verb "help" and the object "you."

questions.question: Am I wanted by you ?[]
options: Did you want me ?
Do you want me ?
Are you wanted me ?
Have you wanted me ?
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Present passive question. To make it active, use the structure: Do/Does + subject (you) + base verb (want) + object (me)?

questions.question: The teacher will be teaching us.[]
options: We shall be taught by the teacher.
We will be taught by the teacher.
We shall be being taught by the teacher.
We will be being taught by the teacher.
questions.explanation: This is the Future Continuous tense. The passive structure is: Subject (We) + shall/will + be + being + V3 (taught) + by + agent (the teacher).

questions.question: Karim told Rahim to give up smoking.[]
options: Rahim was told to give up smoking.
Karim was told to give up smoking.
Rahim is told to give up smoking.
Karim requested Rahim to give up smoking.
questions.explanation: In sentences with an infinitive object ("to give up"), we change the main clause to passive: Object (Rahim) + was + V3 (told). The rest of the sentence remains as is.

questions.question: He teaches us English.[]
options: English was taught us by him.
English is taught us by him.
English is teaching us by him.
English was teaching us by him.
questions.explanation: This sentence has two objects (us, English). Using the direct object as the subject in the Simple Present: Subject (English) + is + V3 (taught) + indirect object (us) + by + agent (him).

questions.question: What did they pay you for doing the job ?[]
options: What did you been paid for doing the job ?
What you were paid for doing the job ?
What were you paid for doing the job ?
What were you being paid for doing the job ?
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Past question. The object "you" becomes the subject, requiring the auxiliary "were." The agent "by them" is omitted because it is general/understood.

questions.question: He satisfied everybody. (Passive)[]
options: Everybody has been satisfied by him.
Everybody was satisfied by him.
Everybody was satisfied with him.
Everybody would be satisfied at him.
questions.explanation: In the Simple Past, "satisfied" becomes "was satisfied." Certain verbs like "satisfy" take the preposition "with" instead of "by" in the passive voice.

questions.question: The sudden noise frightened the horse.[]
options: The sudden horse frightened by the noise.
The noise frightened the horse suddenly.
The horse frightened the noise suddenly.
The horse was frightened by the sudden noise.
questions.explanation: A standard Simple Past conversion: Object (The horse) + was + V3 (frightened) + by + agent (the sudden noise).

questions.question: Who will pay him ?[]
options: Who will be paid him ?
Who would be paid him ?
By whom you will be paid ?
By whom will he be paid ?
questions.explanation: For "Who" in the Simple Future, the passive structure is: By whom + will + subject (he) + be + V3 (paid)?

questions.question: Who is creating the mess ?[]
options: Who has been created the mess ?
By whom has this mess been created ?
By whom this mess is being created ?
By whom is this mess being created ?
questions.explanation: This is Present Continuous. Structure: By whom + is + object (this mess) + being + V3 (created)?

questions.question: Health should be taken care of.[]
options: We should take care of one's health.
One should take care of one's health.
We should take care of ones health.
We must take care of our health.
questions.explanation: When the agent is unspecified in a passive modal sentence ("should be taken"), we use the indefinite pronoun "One" as the subject in the active voice.

questions.question: He did not give up the fight even though he was badly bruised.[]
options: The fight did not give up by him even though he was badly bruised.
The fight had not given up by him even though he was badly bruised.
The fight was not given up by him even though he was badly bruised.
The fight was not giving up by him even though he was badly bruised.
questions.explanation: We convert the first clause (Simple Past Negative): Object (The fight) + was not + V3 (given up) + by + agent (him). The secondary clause remains unchanged.

questions.question: Who killed the bird ? (Passive)[]
options: Who was killed the bird ?
By whom the bird was killed ?
Who was the bird killed by ?
By whom was killed the bird ?
questions.explanation: This is a variation of the passive question format. Instead of starting with "By whom," it uses: Who + auxiliary (was) + object (the bird) + V3 (killed) + by?

questions.question: Shubho ate four pieces of Hilsha fish at dinner. (Passive)[]
options: Four pieces of Hilsha fish at dinner were ate by Shubho.
At dinner four pieces of Hilsha fish Shubho ate.
Four pieces of Hilsha fish were eating by Shubho at dinner.
Four pieces of Hilsha fish were eaten at dinner by Shubho.
questions.explanation: Simple Past conversion. Since "Four pieces" is plural, we use the plural auxiliary "were" followed by the past participle "eaten."

questions.question: Whom were you calling ? (Passive)[]
options: Who called by you ?
Who was being called by you ?
Who are you called ?
Who were you being called ?
questions.explanation: structure:By whom + am/is/are + object + ing + v3+ question mark

questions.question: It is time to stop the shop.(passive)[]
options: It is time for the shop to be stopped.
It is time for the shop to stop.
It is time that the shop should be stopped.
None
questions.explanation: For sentences beginning with "It is time," the passive structure is: It is time + for + object (the shop) + to be + past participle (stopped).
